{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-9098.26","title":"radio.py: record_collision omits channel/time_us; per-channel counts stay empty","description":"## Problem

`Metrics.record_collision` optionally takes `channel` and `time_us`. Those fill `_collisions_by_channel` and `_time_series`. `snapshot()` / `export_csv` / dashboard expose per-channel collisions.

The only production caller is `RadioMixin._get_rx_result_internal`:

    self._metrics.record_collision(node_id, tx_ids)

It already has `channel = node.get_hop_channel()` and `self._current_time_us` in scope and passes `time_us` to the debug log and `on_collision` observer — but not to Metrics.

Result: after a real radio collision, `metrics.collisions >= 1` and `collisions_by_node` increment, but `collisions_by_channel` is `{}` and CSV has no collision rows. `test_metrics.py` `test_collision_without_channel` documents the empty-channel path; `test_radio.py` `test_callback_collision_updates_metrics_and_observer` only checks `collisions == 1`. Hopping / CCP-12 collision isolation cannot be observed from Metrics.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py (`record_collision` call ~L626)
- python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py (`record_collision` channel/time_us kwargs)
- python/tests/sim/test_radio.py (`test_callback_collision_updates_metrics_and_observer`)

## Why this is robustness

Per-channel collision counts are how hopping is validated under load.
